html:
Nursultan Nazarbayev was the first president of independent Kazakhstan, ruling from 1991 to 2019.

He began as a steel worker and rose through the Communist Party. In 1989, after the Jeltoqsan protests, Moscow made him party leader of the Kazakh republic, and he led it to independence when the Soviet Union broke up in 1991.

  • He closed the Semipalatinsk nuclear test site in 1991 and gave up the Soviet nuclear weapons left in the country.
  • He opened the oil fields to Western companies such as Tengizchevroil, and the economy grew fast in the 2000s.
  • He moved the capital from Almaty to Astana in 1997.
  • He kept tight control: elections were not free, and he held the title "Leader of the Nation".

In 2019 he handed the presidency to Kassym-Jomart Tokayev but kept great power. He lost most of it after the January unrest of 2022.
sum: Nursultan Nazarbayev was the first president of independent Kazakhstan, ruling from 1991 to 2019.
